title: Threat intelligence: which warnings deserve your time, and what do you do with them?
short: Subscribe to CERT-Bund, the KEV catalogs and your vendors' advisories, and give every warning that matches your inventory an owner and a decision within one working day.
answer: This month, write down the products, suppliers and sector you need warnings about, and subscribe to the free sources that cover them: CERT-Bund's WID, CISA's and ENISA's catalogs of exploited vulnerabilities and your vendors' advisories. Give every warning that matches your inventory an owner and a decision (patch, block, hunt or detect) within one working day, and judge your intelligence by the actions it produced, not by what you read.
audience: IT and security teams in EU organizations of any size, many in Germany, from teams without analysts to those with a small SOC

blocks.title: If you only do five things

items.title: Write down what you need to know.
items.text: List your internet-facing products and versions, critical suppliers, sector and countries. A warning that touches none of them is reading, not work.

items.title: Subscribe to the free primary sources.
items.text: Register for CERT-Bund's WID, which emails advisories free of charge to match a profile you maintain[^wid]. Add CISA KEV[^kev], ENISA's EU KEV[^enisavs] and your vendors' advisories.

items.title: Filter by your inventory, then act on every match.
items.text: CERT-Bund issued 4,250 advisories in 2026 by 5 November, 55% more than in all of 2025[^widcsaf]. CISA added 284 KEV entries[^kev]: few enough to check each one.

items.title: Detect techniques, not just indicators.
items.text: The NCSC warns that indicators from attackers' covert networks "disappear as quickly as they are discovered"[^ncsccovert]. Build lasting detections on the behavior an advisory describes[^mtrends].

items.title: Join one sharing community.
items.text: In Germany, the Allianz für Cyber-Sicherheit is free[^acs] and passes on the BSI's confidential TLP-labeled warnings[^csw]. Elsewhere, ask your national CERT or your sector's ISAC.

blocks.title: Turn a warning into an action

items.title: Does it touch something on your list?
items.text: Match product, version and exposure against the inventory. CSAF, the JSON format CERT-Bund and many vendors use, lets a tool match advisories against an asset list or SBOM[^csaf][^widcsaf].

items.title: Is it being exploited?
items.text: Check KEV, EU KEV and the advisory. Verizon found the chance of renewed exploitation roughly halves 30 days after the last observed activity[^dbir], so weigh recent activity over an old listing.

items.title: Which action fits?
items.text: Patch or contain within the patching sheet's deadlines. Block indicators that are recent and specific. Hunt in your logs back to the first known exploitation. Add a detection when the advisory describes a technique your logs can show.

items.title: Who does it, and did it hold?
items.text: Open a ticket with one owner and a due date. Close it with the outcome (patched, blocked, nothing found or not affected) once a check confirms it.

blocks.title: Decide what you need to know
items: **Your technology.** Edge devices, identity, remote access and what suppliers run for you. Where ENISA knew the vector of an unauthorized access incident in the EU in 2025, 60.4% used a vulnerability[^etl].

**Your sector and region.** Public administration, business services, transport, manufacturing and finance were the most targeted EU sectors, and ideology-driven operations made up 57.3% of incidents[^etl].
**Your suppliers and your own alerts.** Add your MSP and cloud suppliers, and feed phishing reports and blocked sign-ins back in.

**Strategic reports, once a year.** Read your sector's part of the ENISA Threat Landscape[^etl], the BSI's Lagebericht[^bsilage] and M-Trends or the DBIR. Take one or two changes in priority from each.

blocks.title: Free sources worth subscribing to
items: **CERT-Bund's WID.** Advisories, short notes and warnings by email, tailored to a profile you manage[^wid], and a CSAF feed for automation[^widcsaf].
**CISA KEV and ENISA's EU KEV.** KEV lists 1,768 exploited vulnerabilities[^kev]. EU KEV lists those EU CSIRTs and ENISA confirmed exploited against EU entities[^enisavs].
**Vendor advisories.** Subscribe for every product on your list. NIS2's rules for digital providers require reviewing such channels at planned intervals[^nis2ir].
**The BSI-Portal and the ACS.** Participants get BSI security notices (BITS), warnings and daily and monthly situation reports[^acsportal].
**Microsoft Defender threat analytics.** With any Defender license except Defender for Endpoint P1, reports show your vulnerable devices and the fixes, with email updates[^msta].

blocks.title: Indicators, techniques and ATT&CK
items: **Indicators expire.** Hashes, IP addresses and domains are the easiest things for an attacker to change; techniques are the costliest[^pop]. Give each blocked indicator an expiry date, such as 30 days for IP addresses.
**Search the past.** When an advisory lists indicators, search your logs back to the campaign's start. A hit means incident response, not just a block.
**Build lasting detections on behavior.** Mandiant advises it because attackers rapidly change infrastructure and run malware in memory[^mtrends].
**Tag rules with ATT&CK technique IDs.** Start from the detection strategies MITRE has linked to techniques since v18[^attack18], but don't chase 100% coverage[^attres].

blocks.title: Share what you see
items: **The law expects it.** NIS2 Article 29 has member states let entities share indicators, TTPs and alerts in sharing arrangements, including with suppliers[^nis2]. DORA Article 45 covers financial entities[^dora].
**Personal data needs a basis.** NIS2 recital 121 says legitimate interest under GDPR Article 6(1)(f) can cover sharing IP addresses, URLs and email addresses[^nis2].
**Tell the authority when you join,** as NIS2 and DORA require[^nis2][^dora]. In Germany, BSIG § 30(7) says sharing on the BSI's platform adds no obligations[^bsig].
**Label with TLP 2.0.** CLEAR is public, GREEN stays in the community, AMBER in your organization and its clients, AMBER+STRICT in your organization, RED with named recipients[^tlp].

blocks.title: Is it changing anything?
items: **Actions per month.** Patches, blocks, hunts and detections that started from a warning. Drop any source that produced none for two quarters.
**Time from advisory to decision.** For warnings that match your list. Aim for one working day.
**Learned too late.** Exploited flaws in your products you first heard about from a customer, supplier or the news.

blocks.title: What changed in 2026
items: **The ACS moved into the BSI-Portal.** Existing participants must re-register there by 31 January 2027 or lose their participation[^acsportal].
**ATT&CK split Defense Evasion** into Stealth and Defense Impairment in v19, April 2026[^attack19]. Re-tag rules mapped to the old tactic.
**Manufacturers' reports now feed EU KEV.** CRA reports of exploited vulnerabilities, required since 11 September 2026, will further enrich it[^enisavs].

blocks.title: What you can skip
items: **Paid feeds before free ones turn into tickets.** Only 26% of KEV vulnerabilities in Verizon's data were fully fixed in 2025, after a median of 43 days[^dbir].
**Indicator lists without context.** Without campaign, date and confidence you can't judge them, and IP lists go stale fast[^ncsccovert].
**Tracking actor names.** Microsoft lists 12 other names for its Forest Blizzard, APT28 among them[^msnames]. Track techniques instead.
**A threat intelligence platform before a process.** A mailbox, a ticket queue and a one-page requirements list come first.

blocks.title: Mistakes that cost the most
items: **Reading without a ticket.** A warning that ends in a chat has no owner. Every match gets a ticket, even when the answer is "not affected".
**Blocking feeds unfiltered.** Feeds can include public DNS resolvers, popular domains and scanners. Check them against MISP's warninglists[^mispwl].
**Forwarding labeled warnings to suppliers.** TLP:AMBER covers your organization and its clients, not your MSP. Ask the source first[^tlp].
**Stale subscriptions.** Update the WID profile and vendor subscriptions whenever you add a product.

blocks.title: What this looks like at your size

columns.title: Small team, no security staff
items: Register for WID with a profile for your internet-facing products, sent to a mailbox two people read.
Join the ACS, or your national CERT's community.
Ask your IT provider which advisories it acted on last month.

columns.title: Growing, with IT or security staff
items: Pull KEV, EU KEV and vendor CSAF feeds into tickets, matched against the inventory.
Add one detection a month from an advisory relevant to your sector.
Run MISP, which is free and open source[^misp], or use your ISAC's.

columns.title: Enterprise or regulated
items: Review intelligence requirements with risk owners every quarter.
Register the sharing arrangements you join and the notifications you made.
Put TLP handling in your MSSP contract and report the three measures to leadership.

changes.text: First draft, based on NIS2, DORA, the BSIG, TLP 2.0, the CERT-Bund, CISA and ENISA feeds, ATT&CK and the 2026 reports from ENISA, Mandiant and Verizon.
